newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China shareholder seen key for HK Telecom.
newsitem.headline: China shareholder seen key for HK Telecom.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd shares have staged a rally in recent weeks after months of lagging the market, but analysts said on Tuesday that obtaining a strong Chinese shareholder was key to its future.

Hong Kong reverts to China on midnight of June 30, 1997, and announcing a strategic mainland investor before that date would alleviate the political uncertainty surrounding the company's shares, analysts said.
"It would lift the political cloud that investors perceive over the stock now," said Lloyd Fischer, regional telecommunications analyst at BZW Asia.

"Three things are going to drive the price higher over the next year: the potential for a deal with a strong Chinese entity, reporting of results that show impact from competition but not that significant, and if the company were to return some of its excess liquidity to shareholders," he said.
Fredson Bowers, director of Asia telecoms research at W.I. Carr, said ties to China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications or a related company would be a major plus.
"Our view is in the worst case scenario, the stock is a market performer but with 20 to 30 percent upside if there were to be a change in the shareholder structure," he said.

"That would be a very, very significant lift for Hong Kong Telecom. That would provide some basis for a return of the China premium in the stock. These are issues which will have a much greater impact on the share than a swing in earnings growth."
Recent gains in Hong Kong Telecom shares sparked speculation that CITIC Pacific Ltd may take the opportunity to cut its eight percent stake in the firm.
CITIC Pacific managing director Henry Fan declined to comment.
Hong Kong Telecom shares are currently trading at levels about 11 percent higher than at the end of August. They closed at HK$14.35 (US$1.86) on Monday.

CITIC Pacific, the Hong Kong branch of Beijing's official foreign trading arm China International Trust and Investment Corp, reduced its stake to eight percent from 10 percent in June and said it had decided to refocus its investment strategy.
Analysts said it would make sense for CITIC Pacific to further reduce its stake and a mainland Chinese company would be a good replacement.

Analysts said Hong Kong Telecom shares now looked fairly valued, with concerns about increased competition and its ties to Britain reflected in the price. Britain's Cable & Wireless Plc owns about 58 percent of Hong Kong Telecom.
"The key question is can a British company continue to control Hong Kong Telecom post 1997. I think it is looking increasingly unlikely," said Bowers.

Other major blue chip colonial firms have been establishing ties with mainland firms. Swire Pacific Ltd teamed up with CITIC Pacific and its Cathay Pacific Airlines Ltd is also 25-percent owned by CITIC.

"It is very important from an investor perception that Hong Kong Telecom is seen to have mainland China on its side. I think it would certainly help the share greatly if the mainland was firmly behind Hong Kong Telecom," said David Gibbons, regional telecoms analyst for HSBC James Capel Asia.
